text:
Predicates:
NearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Rabbit(x) ::: x is a rabbit.
Cute(x) ::: x is cute.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
CanBeSpottedNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Squirrel(x) ::: x is a squirrel.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Rockie ::: individual named Rockie.

Premises:
∀x (NearCampus(x) ∧ Rabbit(x)) → Cute(x) ::: All rabbits near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ NearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x ((Rabbit(x) ∨ Squirrel(x)) ∧ CanBeSpottedNearCampus(x)) ::: The only animals that can be spotted near the campus are rabbits and squirrels.
∀x (Skittish(x) → ¬Calm(x)) ::: If something is skittish, then it is not calm.
∀x (CanBeSpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Squirrel(x)) → Skittish(x) ::: All squirrels near the campus are skittish.
CanBeSpottedNearCampus(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus.
Calm(Rockie) ::: Rockie is calm.

Conclusion:
(¬(Turtle(Rockie) ∧ Squirrel(Rockie))) → (Cute(Rockie) ∨ Skittish(Rockie))) ::: If Rockie is not both a turtle and a squirrel, then Rockie is either cute or skittish.
